content: The Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) is a division of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) that oversees the production and distribution of food, food additives, and drugs intended for use in animals. This includes animals that are sources of human food, as well as pets and companion animals. CVM is tasked with regulating drugs, medical devices, and food additives that are administered to or used on over 100 million companion animals, in addition to millions of poultry, cattle, swine, and minor animal species. Minor animal species refer to animals other than cattle, swine, chickens, turkeys, horses, dogs, and cats. The official CVM logo is used on various publications and printed materials that are authorized by the Center for Veterinary Medicine. CVM is responsible for monitoring the safety of animal food products, issuing safety warnings, and redistributing recall notices when necessary.
